A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and include the theory and experimental appendices. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable matching across reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B report original LLM fine-tuning evaluations and ablations on instruction-following and academic benchmarks.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B retain those original experimental results, including reward augmentation, feedback-quality, and reward-conditioning evaluations.

M1.justification: Reward-conditioned preference relabeling, construction of two pairs per original pair, subsequent DPO, and inference at the maximum reward goal are unchanged. The RA+ and multi-attribute variants already appear in v3.

E1.justification: Both use offline and on-policy UltraFeedback data, AlpacaEval 2.0, MT-Bench, Arena-Hard-Auto, and the same six academic benchmarks. The evaluated scenarios remain present across main-text and appendix moves.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched experiments, including the on-policy baselines in v3 Table 8/v4 Table 12 and conditional fine-tuning baselines in Figure 4. New related-work citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 changes the reported batch size from 128 to 256 while retaining beta = 0.01. This revises a stated training setting; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The data-utility, dataset-size, unlearning, feedback-quality, multi-attribute, prompt-control, rejected-response filtering, and reward-scale analyses are retained. Feedback-quality analysis moves to Appendix B.3, while prompt-control analysis moves into Section 6.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The statistical reporting in the matched experimental tables and figures is unchanged.

E6.justification: All 15 table bodies match after renumbering, including their numerical entries, and the plotted findings are retained. For example, the multi-attribute model retains 56.57 length-controlled win rate and 52.19 win rate in v3 Table 9/v4 Table 7.

T1.justification: The reward definitions, theoretical algorithm, assumptions, convergence bounds, and appendix proofs are unchanged. References incorrectly naming Algorithm 8 are corrected to Algorithm 1 without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract is shortened, but the paper retains its contributions and claims about reward-conditioned relabeling, improved alignment and data utility, reduced unlearning, and generalization to high-quality responses. The on-policy state-of-the-art claim remains in the introduction.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly states that UltraFeedback lacks textual feedback and uses this to explain restricting comparisons with textual-feedback alignment to reward-feedback variants. Existing interpretations concerning unlearning, feedback noise, and reward scaling remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly documents searches over beta values [0.001, 0.01, 0.1] and batch sizes [64, 128, 256], and explicitly states that the proposed method shares DPO's hyperparameters. The code address, underlying prompt text, optimizer, learning rate, and label-smoothing details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds focused positioning against ULMA, Decision Transformer, iterative reasoning preference optimization, textual-feedback alignment, and margin-matching preference optimization. These additions clarify distinctions from prior methods while retaining the central positioning as data relabeling without algorithm modifications.

P1.justification: v4 condenses the abstract, edits prose, expands related work, adds an Impact Statement, and moves several experimental discussions between Section 6.2 and Appendix B.3. The main section sequence remains intact. Some cross-references are corrected, but the multi-attribute discussion's references to the 'last part' no longer point to the relocated feedback setup.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures and tables. Appendix B.1 replaces wrapped, boxed prompts with unwrapped lines that run off the right page edge; their full wording remains extractable from the PDF.

improvement.justification: v4 improves research positioning and documents hyperparameter selection more clearly. However, its layout clips both Appendix B.1 prompt examples, and relocating the feedback setup leaves misleading 'last part' references in Section 6.2. With the scientific method, theory, and results unchanged, these documentation gains and readability losses do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
